subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public web-tool egress boundary be for domain allow/deny controls: scoped web_fetch policy, cross-tool search/fetch/browser policy, or managed-proxy-owned egress?
rationale: This would create an operator-trusted security/config surface, and current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping deny-domain, search, browser, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Design Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Pause narrow local knobs and define one cross-tool contract for fetch, search, browser, providers, plugins, redirects, caches, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy As Boundary
options.body: Route application-owned egress policy through proxy.enabled and external operator policy instead of adding local domain firewall semantics to web tools.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping deny-domain, search, browser, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across guarded fetch, SSRF helpers, web_fetch runtime/docs, and prior URL allowlist rollback/refactor decisions.
